stemBlocks.value: Make r the subject of the formula V = 4πr³/3 (the volume of a sphere).
Think first: r is cubed, so the last step will be a cube root, not a square root.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p096-q12 from workbook page 96.

solutionSteps.instruction: Take the cube root of both sides.

contentBlocks.value: The inverse of cubing is the cube root

strategyBlocks.value: Multiply by 3, divide by 4π to isolate r³, then take the cube root of both sides.

whyThisWorks.value: Each operation applied to r — cubing, multiplying by 4π, dividing by 3 — is undone in reverse order. The cube root is left until last because it can only be applied once r³ stands alone; taking it earlier would trap the other factors inside the root.

commonErrors.misconception: Taking a square root instead of a cube root.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Taking a square root instead of a cube root.

commonErrors.misconception: Applying the cube root before isolating r³, giving r = ∛(3V)/4π.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Applying the cube root before isolating r³, giving r = ∛(3V)/4π.
Avoid this: Multiplying by 4π instead of dividing.

examTip.value: A power on the subject always comes off last: clear fractions, divide out coefficients, and only then root both sides.
